name: SecretsVault
purpose: Fetch, cache, rotate, and audit application secrets through a named-secret interface backed by an external key management or secrets service.
api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SecretVersion:
    name: str
    version: int
    material: bytes
    not_after: int | None

class SecretsVault(Protocol):
    def get(self, name: str) -> SecretVersion: ...
    def rotate(self, name: str) -> SecretVersion: ...
    def invalidate(self, name: str) -> None: ...
invariants: Secret material MUST NEVER be logged, included in tracebacks, or serialized to telemetry.
get() MUST honor a time-bounded cache; cached material MUST NEVER outlive not_after or the configured max-age.
rotate() MUST produce a strictly increasing version and MUST NEVER return the same material for a different version.
Every get()/rotate() call SHALL emit a structured audit event naming the secret (not the material) and the caller identity.
When the underlying backend is unavailable, the vault MUST fail closed for cold secrets and CANNOT surface stale material past its cache TTL.
extension_contract: Backends register as vault adapters (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, GCP Secret Manager, filesystem-for-dev) implementing the Protocol. An adapter is refused if it cannot produce a monotonically increasing version identifier or does not support rotation callbacks.
why_essential: Secrets scattered in environment variables and config files rotate on no one's schedule; a shared vault primitive makes rotation, caching, and audit a single policy decision rather than a per-service migration.
alternatives_considered: Env vars injected at deploy — no rotation, no audit, leaks into crash dumps.
Per-service SDK call — inconsistent caching and blast-radius controls.
Encrypted config file checked into repo — key management problem reappears one level down.
